(B.C.CHANDRASHEKAR)
 XXIV A.C.M.M., BENGALURU.
: J U D G M E N T :

The PI of Vijayanagar Police station has filed chargesheet against accused No.1 and 2 for the offence punishable u/s.392 r/w.34 of IPC.
 2.

The brief facts of the case of the prosecution are that on 2/6/17 at 3.20 pm., while CW.1 along with her son were going in her Suzuki Access vehicle near 5 th cross,
G.K.W.layout, Vijayanagar within the jurisdiction of Vijayanagar Police Station, the accused persons came on motor cycle opposite to CW 1, at that time, the CW 1 did not get balance and fell down on the ground, then the accused no.2 snatched gold mangalya chain and a plain chain from  3 CC.No.10119/18 the neck of CW.1 worth Rs.1,72,000/ weighing 72 grams and ran away from the spot and thereby have committed an offence punishable U/sec.392 r/w.34 of IPC.
 3.
On the basis of the complaint of the CW 1, this crime has been registered by Vijayanagar Police Station.
During the crime stage, since the accused persons were in JC in some other case, body warrant was issued against them.
After investigation, Investigating officer has submitted the chargesheet against the accused No.1 and 2 for the offence u/s.392 r/w.34 of IPC.
The cognizance for the said offences are taken.
Later on accused No.1 and 2 have filed the bail application through their counsel & accordingly, they have released on bail.
4. The copies of the prosecution papers have furnished to the accused no.1 and 2 as contemplated u/s.207 of Cr.P.C.,

After being heard the arguments before charge, as there were no grounds to discharge them, charge for the offences u/s.392 r/w.34 of IPC have been framed & read over, explained to the Accused No.1 and 2 in the language best known to them.
The Accused No.1 and 2 have not pleaded guilty and claims to be tried.
Hence, the case taken up for trial.
At this juncture, accused no.1 did not appear before the court.
Inspite of issue of number of NBWs, the  4 CC.No.10119/18 presence of accused no.1 could not be secured.

Hence, case against accused no.1 is ordered to be split up vide orders dtd:

2 04/07/2022.
 5.

sentences.text: In order to prove the guilt of the accused no.2, the prosecution has examined 5 witnesses as PW 1 to 5 out of 16 witnesses as cited in the chargesheet.
4 documents have been marked as Ex.P.1 to 4.
After prosecution evidence, the accused no.2 has been examined u/s.313 of Cr.P.C., & he has denied the prosecution evidence.
The accused no.2 has not chosen to submit the defence evidence.
6. Heard the arguments of learned APP and counsel for accused no.2.
Perused,
On the basis of the above, the following points have arises for my consideration :

1) Whether prosecution proves beyond  reasonable doubt that on 2/6/17 at  3.20 pm., while CW.1 along with her  son were going in her Suzuki Access  vehicle near 5th cross, G.K.W.layout,
 Vijayanagar within the jurisdiction of  Vijayanagar Police Station, the accused  persons came on motor cycle opposite to  CW 1, at that time, the CW 1 did not get  balance and fell down on the ground,
 then the accused no.2 snatched gold  mangalya chain and a plain chain from  the neck of CW.1 worth Rs.1,72,000/
 weighing 72 grams and ran away from  5 CC.No.10119/18  the spot and thereby have committed an  offence punishable U/sec.392 r/w.34  of IPC ?
 2) What order?
 7. My answer to the above points is as under;
 Point No.1 In the Negative  Point No.2As per final order for the following :
 REASONS  8.
According to the prosecution, accused No.2 has committed an offence u/s.392 r/w.34 of IPC.
In order to prove the guilt of the accused no.2, the prosecution has examined the complainant as PW.1, who is the victim.

The PW 1 has deposed that on 2/6/17 at 3.15 pm., after pick up of her son from school, when she was going on her two wheeler near Vyalikaval road, some unknown persons came opposite to her vehicle, at that time, she and her son fell down from the vehicle and when she was about to get up, those persons snatched her 2 gold chains weighing 72 grams and The State Of Karnataka Through vs 2. Arunkumar @ Aruna on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142340260/
3 ran away.

entities.text: State Of Karnataka Through vs 2. Arunkumar @ Aruna
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, she has lodged the complaint as per Ex.P.1.
She further deposed that on the same day, the police drew spot mahazar as per Ex.P.2 in the presence of CW 2 and 3.
After 10 days of the incident, the police called her to the Police Station and showed her lost gold chains, she identified the same and got released the same.
Further she deposed that the  6 CC.No.10119/18 police have not shown any accused persons, she does not know who have snatched her gold chains and she has not given any statement.
Thus she has turned hostile to the case of the prosecution.
9. At request of learned senior APP this witness has been treated as hostile witness and permission was accorded to cross examine him.
In the cross examination the learned Sr.APP suggested that on 13/7/17 police called her to the Police Station to identify the accused persons and same has been denied by the witness.

According to the prosecution when the CW 1 has fallen down the accused no.2 before the court has snatched her 72 grams chain but she has not identified the accused no.2 before the court as a person who snatched her chain.
Since the complainant being the victim though she has deposed about snatching of her chain, she has not identified the accused no.2 before the court as one of the person who snatched the chain.
Hence, the strong doubt accrued in the mind of the court about the case of the prosecution.
Hence, the prosecution is required to prove the guilt of the accused persons by examining other material witnesses.

10. The prosecution has examined the spot mahazar witness CW 2 as PW 2 and he has deposed that on 2/6/17  7 CC.No.10119/18 near G.K.Layout, with regard to chain snatching, the police have came near the spot and drew the mahazar as per Ex.P.2.
 11.

Similarly, the prosecution has examined another spot mahazar witness CW 3 as PW 3 and he has deposed that on 2/6/17 near G.K.Layout, with regard to chain snatching,
the police have came near the spot and drew the mahazar as per Ex.P.2.
Thus, the PW 2 and 3 being the spot mahazar witnesses have deposed about drawing up of the spot mahazar at the spot as per Ex.P.2.
But merely because the mahazar witness have deposed about the drawing up of the mahazar, it does not means to say that the accused persons have committed the offence.
Hence, the prosecution is required to prove the guilt of the accused no.2 by examining the other material witnesses.

sentences.text: The prosecution has further examined one of the IO who registered the crime as PW 4 and he has deposed that on 2/6/17, he was on SHO duty, at about 4.00 pm., CW 1 came and lodged the complaint as per Ex,P.1, hence, he has registered the crime in Cr.No.276/17 and sent FIR to the court and his higher officers and handed over case papers to CW16.

Accordingly PW 4 being one of the Investigating officer has just deposed about registration of the crime, hence, there is no any material allegation against the accused no.2.
 8 CC.No.10119/18  13.

The prosecution has further examined another IO CW 16 as PW 5, he has deposed that on 2/6/17 he has received the case papers from CW 15 and deputed the staff to trace the accused persons and on the same day, in between 5 to 6 pm., he drew up the spot mahazar as per Ex.P.2.
Later on the Jayanagar police have caught hold the accused persons and as well as snatched jewelries and it has given to its owner.
Since the accused persons are in JC in some other case, on 25/7/17 he has requested the court to issue body warrant.
On 11/10/17 he has collected the documents from Jayanagar police and after investigation he has filed the final report.

Thus, the PW 5 being one of the Investigating officer who filed the final report has just deposed about drawing up of the mahazar and receiving of the documents from the Jayanagar police about arrest of the accused persons and recovery of snatched articles and filed the final report.
But he has not conducted any investigation against the accused persons and he has not arrested them and not seized any articles from them.
Hence, the evidence of PW 5 is not disclosing the material allegation against the accused no.2.

The Investigating officer who arrested the accused persons and seized the snatched articles from the possession of the accused persons or on their information will play an important role in proving the guilt of the accused persons as  9 CC.No.10119/18 well as the mahazar witnesses who were present at the time of recovery of chain will also play an important role in proving the guilt of the accused persons.
Hence, it is just and necessary to look over the other evidence.
14. Apart from the oral evidence, Ex.P.1 is the complaint, Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.3 is the statement of the PW 1, Ex.P.4 is the FIR.

15 . It is significant to note here that this court has issued number of Summons, NBW including proclamation to CW 6 to 14, but Investigating officer has failed to execute the The State Of Karnataka Through vs 2. Arunkumar @ Aruna on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142340260/
5 same and keep present the material witnesses as well as Investigating officers before the court.

sentences.text: Hence, with no option CW 6 to 14 have dropped with a liberty to the prosecution to produce the witnesses at any time without filing any recall application.
Inspite of that the prosecution has not make use of the opportunity and examined the other material witnesses.
Thus, there is a lacking of material evidence to accept the guilt of the accused no.2.

PW 1 complainant though deposed about chain snatching, she has not identified the accused no.2 before the court, PW 2 and 3 being spot mahazar witnesses have deposed about drawing up of the mahazar and PW 4 and 5 being the Investigating officers have deposed about their investigation.
But their evidence is not sufficient  10 CC.No.10119/18 to believe that the accused no.2 has snatched the chain of the PW 1.
Accordingly, the evidence placed by the prosecution is not sufficient to believe the guilt of the accused no.2 beyond all reasonable doubt.
With the above discussion, since there is lacking of evidence, I am unable to accept that the accused no.2 has committed the offences as alleged in the prosecution.
In a criminal justice system, if a tiny doubt arises in the mind of the court, benefit of doubt shall be extended to the accused no.2.
In this case, not only tiny doubt but the strong doubt arise in the mind of the court, because the victim herself has not supported the case of the prosecution.
Hence, the prosecution has utterly failed to prove the guilt of the accused no.2 beyond all reasonable doubt.
Hence, in my opinion it is a fit case to extend benefit of doubt to the accused no.2.
Accordingly point under reference answered in the Negative.
16. POINT NO.2 :

For the aforesaid reason and discussion, I proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. Accused No.2 is hereby acquitted for the offence punishable U/s.392 r/w.34 of IPC.
The bail bond executed by the accused No.2 are stands cancelled.
However, Accused No.2 shall execute personal bond of Rs.50,000/ by undertaking to appear before the appellate Court, if any appeal is filed.

It is not a fit case to award victim compensation as provided U/s.357(1) of Cr.P.C.,
Office is directed to keep the original file and property in split up case registered against accused No.1.
(Dictated to the stenographer, script transcribed by her and then corrected directly on computer and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 21 st day of January 2023).
(B.C.Chandrashekar) XXIV A.C.M.M., BENGALURU.
